items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: Well, Ellis Stratikas is playing, Ellis was living in Gulfport at this time, I believe his dad had a confectionary or something over there. Well anyway, when Ellis was playing with Johnny...

ctx.x: What Shillin is that? George Happy.

That's Happy, not his son. Oh, no, no, well, this is a long time ago. Yeah. And, yeah, I worked there. Yeah, he had, and then of course when Happy, a lot of times Happy Shillin used to get two jobs, and Johnny Lollard, Johnny was the fellow who played the jazz, the hornet, you know, and he also played a little piano, too cool to think. And when he got two jobs, of course this was, if I wasn't working, of course in the daytime I couldn't make them, and picnics and things like that. Well I used to play with the…
I was going to ask you, it had Imperial Jazz on the drum, in that picture of Johnny Batusi's band? Yeah. And Ellis is playing the drums, Ellis Stratikas.

items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: Yeah, Stratica was about one of the few bands that I can remember that was up there.

ctx.x: Yeah, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. Don Don played. Funny thing, I believe we had a brother by the name of Harold Peterson too. Yeah, we used to play with all those times. He sure did. We lived on Broadway and they lived on Broadway.
And he used to call out the mall. Oh yeah, that's huge. Did you ever go to the John Roof? Do you hear anybody up there? I don't know, Stratica.

Yeah, Stratica was about one of the few bands that I can remember that was up there. Yeah. Well, they recorded when they were up there. I don't remember anybody that had a band that played up there. I'm just trying to think. I think Stratica was the only band that played up there.
